analysis.title: Europe Food: Chocolate monitor: Q3 read-across from Mondelez and Hershey, expert call feedback, and tracking the data
key_insights: Mondelez Q3 chocolate volume/mix accelerated to +2.8% (Q2: -1.6%) with implied pricing of -2.2% (Q2: +1.5%). European chocolate volume/mix turned positive and management said demand held up in the hotter-than-usual summer. Mondelez confirmed selective price adjustments in Europe earlier in the year.

Hershey expects retail unit and volume trends to improve further in Q4 as investment programmes build and non-seasonal pricing begins to lap. It does not plan to roll back prices and will use targeted promotions and pack/price offerings instead. Seasonal pricing announced earlier continues into 2027.

Hershey plans a 50% increase in innovation across its categories in 2027, with the biggest launches in Q1. Advertising and related consumer marketing rose 17% in Q3. Full-year brand investment is expected up high-single digits, with a step-up in Q4.
Mondelez focuses on absolute gross profit growth, is pleased with how the Europe P&L is progressing, and remains focused on volume growth in Q4 and 2027.

US convenience channel is under pressure: consumers became more deliberate on spending in channels exposed to higher gas prices. The US candy, gum and mint category fell about 5% in convenience per Hershey, and the caution persisted into October. Mondelez sees price sensitivity driving growth in value channels and smaller packs. Consumer confidence is soft on energy and fuel prices and management does not expect that to change near term.
Hershey expects Halloween participation in line with 2025, but visibility is limited because most purchases happen in the final days and financial pressure could affect decisions.
Hershey's guidance implies a larger cocoa cost tailwind in 2027. Management targets a mid-40% gross margin over the long term (Visible Alpha consensus: 41.0% for 2026).

On cocoa supply, Mondelez expects a 500kt surplus in 2025/26 (Hershey: 500-600kt) and a 190kt deficit in 2026/27, driven by a poor Cote d'Ivoire main crop and an expected strong El Nino. Mondelez estimates the industry has covered cocoa needs for the next nine months.

Expert call with Andrej Vouk (REWE): some brands are launching Christmas 2026 promotions early and guaranteeing unsold stock, for example by paying for markdowns. Weak Christmas 2025 sales led retailers to cut Christmas 2026 orders, and Easter 2027 orders have also been cut after a weak Easter 2026. Christmas SKU production cutoffs have passed.

Price gap between private label and branded chocolate has widened from the historical c.40-60% to about 70%. Private label prices fell about 10% while brands did not follow. Vouk expects consumer resistance to push brands to cut prices into 2027, from low-single-digit to double-digit reductions depending on product. Private label chocolate prices could rise in 2027 on higher sugar, energy and freight costs.

Private label now drives 55% of new product development industry-wide, up from 52% five years ago. Consumers are diversifying into protein bars and blended formats, and willingness to pay a premium is becoming more selective.

Cocoa prices have stabilised but GS commodities (Lina Thomas) sees upside risk, because a potential Super El Nino raises the risk of a poor West African crop (about 65% of world supply). Prices have rebounded sharply since April, and in the chart commentary cocoa troughed about 80% below its peak in Feb 26 and has since doubled. Grindings have recovered from the Q1 26 trough.

Nielsen Europe: chocolate volumes -2.3% in the 4 weeks to 4 Oct, with private label volume +2.8% while all major branded manufacturers declined. Market pricing -1.9% vs -0.4% in the 4 weeks to 6 Sep, with private label price cuts accelerating from -2.5% in September to -5.0% in October.

Nielsen US: price/mix moderated to +9% in the 4 weeks to 17 Oct, while market volumes are -9%. Lindt is the exception, with pricing +2%, likely reflecting negative mix as it laps the Dubai-style chocolate launch in H2 2025. Weak US volumes could read negatively for Barry Callebaut, which generates 24% of its volumes in North America.

Barry Callebaut (Neutral, PT CHF1,210) reports FY26 results on 4 November. GS estimates Mondelez, Hershey and Nestle account for 24% of its volumes and forecasts a volume recovery of +2.8% in FY27e. Lindt & Sprungli (Sell) reports FY26 sales on 19 January and earnings on 9 March.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral on Barry Callebaut with FY26 results due 4 November. Weak US volumes (-9% market) are a negative read-across given 24% North America exposure, while GS forecasts a +2.8% volume recovery in FY27e.
Sell on Lindt. Nielsen shows Lindt volumes weak in Europe and the US, and brand price cuts and early cocoa deflation are cited as risks to the Sell view.
Q3 chocolate volume/mix accelerated to +2.8% with Europe turning positive. Nielsen shows Mondelez Europe pricing negative. Covered by Leah Jordan.
Management expects volume trends to improve in Q4 and plans a 50% increase in innovation in 2027. Nielsen shows US volumes down 17% in the 4 weeks to 17 Oct. Covered by Leah Jordan.

sector_views.rationale: Volume demand remains muted in Europe and the US, competition is increasing as private label gains share, and brands may need to cut prices into 2027. Cocoa deflation supports margins but El Nino poses upside price risk.

earnings_insights: Mondelez Q3 chocolate volume/mix +2.8% vs Q2 -1.6%, implied pricing -2.2% vs Q2 +1.5% (company-reported, 3Q26 results already printed).
Hershey Q3 advertising and related consumer marketing +17% (reported). Full-year brand investment guided up high-single digits.
Hershey long-term gross margin target in the mid-40% range vs Visible Alpha consensus of 41.0% for 2026 (consensus estimate).
Barry Callebaut reports FY26 results on 4 November 2026. GS forecasts FY27e volume growth of +2.8%.
Lindt & Sprungli reports FY26 sales on 19 January and FY26 earnings on 9 March.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports cocoa cost deflation for chocolate makers.
A poor Cote d'Ivoire main crop and a strong El Nino would tighten supply and raise price risk.
Muted demand, with private label gaining at the expense of brands.
Pricing remains elevated but is moderating.
Weak demand, a negative read for Barry Callebaut.

risk_factors: Super El Nino could cause a poor West African cocoa crop (about 65% of world supply) and push cocoa prices higher.
Brands may have to cut prices into 2027 as private label price gaps widen to about 70%.
Weak consumer confidence from energy and fuel prices, with pressure in US convenience channels.
Limited visibility on Halloween and seasonal gifting demand, and reduced retailer orders for Christmas 2026 and Easter 2027.
Barry Callebaut: cocoa price changes, demand, execution on Focus for Growth, input cost inflation, supply disruption, FX.
Lindt: raw material deflation arriving earlier than expected, more resilient consumer elasticities, slower industry promotion growth, faster North America recovery, Swiss franc depreciation.

tension_points.bull_case: Mondelez chocolate volume/mix turned to +2.8% in Q3, Hershey expects volume trends to improve in Q4, and cocoa deflation gives room to step up brand and innovation investment.
tension_points.bear_case: Nielsen shows European volumes at -2.3% and US volumes at -9%, private label is taking share, and the retailer expert expects brands to cut prices as price gaps widen.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued Nielsen volume declines for branded players and Barry Callebaut FY26 results on 4 November showing weak volumes would undercut the recovery view.
